# Bunny Stream React Native

> `@bunny.net/stream-react-native` — React Native SDK for Bunny's video
> platform. One TypeScript API over the official iOS/Android SDKs for VOD
> playback, live streaming, camera broadcasting, resumable uploads, and library
> management. New Architecture only (TurboModules + Fabric).

This file is an integration cheat sheet for AI agents and developers. It lists
the rules that are easy to get wrong; follow the linked guides for details.

## Requirements

- React Native with the **New Architecture** enabled. There is no Old
  Architecture fallback — do not generate bridge/legacy code.
- Expo: SDK 52+ **development build** only. Expo Go and web are unsupported.
- iOS 15+, CocoaPods with `spm_dependency` support. Android API 26+,
  `compileSdk` 36+, Kotlin 2.2.20+, core library desugaring enabled.
- A Bunny Stream library ID and API access key.

## Critical integration rules

Read these before writing code — each one is a common failure mode:

1. `initialize(accessKey, libraryId)` must run once at app startup, before
   mounting any player or calling the API. It validates inputs (non-empty key,
   positive integer library ID) before reaching native code.
2. API and upload calls return `Promise<BunnyResult<T>>` and **never reject**.
   Do not rely on try/catch for API errors — check `result.ok`, then use
   `result.value` or `result.error` (`BunnyError` has `kind` and `isTerminal`).
3. `BunnyStreamUpload.startUpload()` defaults to `mode: 'basic'`
   (non-resumable). Set `mode: 'tus'` explicitly for resumable uploads.
   Uploads do **not** auto-retry when connectivity returns — persist the
   video/file details and call `continueUpload()`.
4. Only one `BunnyStreamPlayer` VOD instance can be active at a time (native
   SDK singleton). The component remounts its native host when `source`
   identity changes — never render two players simultaneously.
5. `source.libraryId` is optional on every source type and falls back to the
   library passed to `initialize()`.
6. Request camera and microphone permissions at runtime **before** mounting
   `BunnyStreamBroadcaster` — the SDK declares them but does not request them.
7. Bare-RN iOS consumers must embed `GoogleInteractiveMediaAds.framework`
   (a native-player dependency) via a Run Script phase. The Expo config plugin
   does this automatically; see `plugin/src/ios.ts` for the script.
8. Broadcasting is foreground-only — stop the broadcast when the app goes to
   background.
9. Platform behavior differs: upload pause/resume semantics, background
   uploads (iOS TUS survives termination, Android dies with the process),
   Android TV (`useNativeTvPlayer` + `net.bunny:tv`), broadcaster quality
   configuration. Check JSDoc on the owning API and `docs/guides/` before
   assuming symmetric behavior.
10. Events arrive as component props (`onReady`, `onProgress`, `onError`,
    `onLiveError`, `onStateChange`, …). Upload events go through
    `BunnyStreamUpload.addUploadListener(listener)`, which returns an
    unsubscribe function — call it on cleanup.

## Canonical usage

```ts
import { initialize } from '@bunny.net/stream-react-native';

initialize('your-library-api-key', 12345); // once, at startup
```

```tsx
import { BunnyStreamPlayer } from '@bunny.net/stream-react-native';

// VOD — libraryId optional, falls back to initialize()
<BunnyStreamPlayer
  source={{ type: 'vod', videoId: 'video-guid' }}
  style={{ width: '100%', aspectRatio: 16 / 9 }}
/>

// Live — same component, separate native host
<BunnyStreamPlayer
  source={{ type: 'live', streamId: 'stream-guid' }}
  style={{ width: '100%', aspectRatio: 16 / 9 }}
/>
```

```ts
import { BunnyStreamApi } from '@bunny.net/stream-react-native';

const result = await BunnyStreamApi.listVideos(12345);
if (result.ok) {
  console.log(result.value.items);
} else {
  console.warn(result.error.message, result.error.isTerminal);
}
```

```ts
import { BunnyStreamUpload } from '@bunny.net/stream-react-native';

const result = await BunnyStreamUpload.startUpload({
  libraryId: 12345,
  uri: 'file:///path/to/video.mp4',
  title: 'My video',
  mode: 'tus', // required for resumable uploads
});

const unsubscribe = BunnyStreamUpload.addUploadListener((event) => {
  // progress / completion / failure events
});
```

```tsx
import { BunnyStreamBroadcaster, BunnyImage } from '@bunny.net/stream-react-native';

// Broadcast to an existing live stream (needs runtime cam/mic permission)
<BunnyStreamBroadcaster
  accessKey="your-library-api-key"
  source={{ type: 'live', libraryId: 12345, streamId: 'stream-guid' }}
  onError={(e) => console.warn(e.message)}
/>

// CDN thumbnail with the Referer header hotlink protection requires
<BunnyImage source={{ uri: video.thumbnailUrl }} style={styles.thumb} />
```

## API surface

- `initialize` — `src/config/initialize.ts`
- `BunnyStreamPlayer`, `useBunnyStreamPlayer`, resume-position helpers,
  `isRunningOnTV`, `getPlaybackSpeeds` — `src/player/` (types:
  `src/player/BunnyStreamPlayer.types.ts`)
- `BunnyStreamApi` (videos, collections, live streams, captions, thumbnails,
  reencode, transcription, analytics) + `BunnyResult` helpers — `src/api/`
- `BunnyStreamUpload` — `src/upload/BunnyStreamUpload.ts`
- `BunnyStreamBroadcaster` — `src/broadcaster/`
- `BunnyImage`, `bunnyImageSource`, `useBunnyImage` — `src/image/`

JSDoc on these files is the authoritative API reference — it ships inside the
package's `.d.ts` files.
